_comment: OpenSSF Best Practices badge (passing level) proposed answers for Claustodian. Read by bestpractices.dev when the project entry is edited or re-run with 'Save (and continue)'. Status values: Met | Unmet | N/A ('?' / unknown are ignored, leaving any existing answer unchanged). Justifications are a starting point; the authorized maintainer reviews and confirms each before saving. Project: https://www.bestpractices.dev/en/projects/14130 - Repository: https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian
description_good_justification: The README states up front what Claustodian is - a static, versioned, machine-parseable record of every Claude Code CLI flag, environment variable, command, config key, and stream-json control message, each tagged with the version it first appeared in. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian
interact_justification: Users can ask questions and interact through GitHub Issues. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian/issues
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md at the repository root explains how to contribute, leading with the provenance policy that is the core of the project's trustworthiness. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the requirements: the provenance policy (only material Anthropic has publicly published), every record must validate against schema/symbol.schema.json, local gates before opening a PR (lint, prettier --check, tsc --noEmit, test, validate), branch from a fresh main, PRs target main, and Conventional Commit subjects. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
floss_license_justification: The code is released under the Apache License 2.0, an OSI-approved and FSF-recognized FLOSS license; the dataset is released under CC BY 4.0. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: Apache-2.0 is an OSI-approved open source license.
license_location_justification: The code license is in the standard top-level LICENSE file, and the data license is in LICENSE-DATA. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics_justification: The README, the docs/ directory (architecture and runbooks), and the published site cover what the dataset is, how it is produced, and how to consume it. https://claustodian.dev
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is the published static files (JSON plus generated YAML and TOML) and their record contract; the README documents how to fetch them and schema/symbol.schema.json defines every field. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian/blob/main/schema/symbol.schema.json
sites_https_justification: The repository (github.com), the published dataset site (claustodian.dev, served via GitHub Pages behind Cloudflare), and the API endpoints it fetches are served exclusively over HTTPS.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests provide searchable, URL-addressable discussion that needs no client-side JavaScript. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian/issues
english_justification: All documentation and code comments are in English.
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained; changes ship through reviewed pull requests, and the dataset is regenerated and republished frequently as new Claude Code versions are released.
repo_public_justification: The source is in a public git repository. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian
repo_track_justification: git records what changed, who changed it, and when.
repo_interim_justification: Interim development versions are public between changes as commits and pull requests on GitHub.
repo_distributed_justification: The project uses git, a distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: The project publishes continuously rather than cutting discrete software releases: each deploy is built from a specific main commit (a unique version-controlled identifier), and every published dataset snapshot is itself keyed by the Claude Code version it describes.
version_semver_justification: This criterion does not offer an N/A option. Claustodian follows a continuous-delivery model - the dataset is regenerated from main and republished on each deploy - rather than issuing SemVer-numbered software releases, so it is marked Unmet. The data it contains is versioned by the upstream Claude Code version it records. (SUGGESTED, so it does not block the passing badge.)
version_tags_justification: This criterion does not offer an N/A option. The project does not cut tagged software releases; it publishes continuously from main, so there are no release tags. Consumer-visible changes are recorded in CHANGELOG.md. (SUGGESTED, so it does not block the passing badge.)
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md records human-readable, consumer-visible changes to the dataset and pipeline. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability has been fixed to date; the changelog would record such a fix if one occurred.
report_process_justification: The process for reporting problems is documented: dataset corrections go through GitHub Issues (a dedicated dataset-correction template collects the required evidence), and CONTRIBUTING.md explains the flow. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian/issues
report_tracker_justification: Bugs and dataset corrections are tracked in GitHub Issues.
report_responses_justification: The maintainer monitors the issue tracker and responds; the project is new and has no backlog of unanswered reports.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests filed as GitHub Issues receive a response, including a decision when a request falls outside the project's deliberately narrow scope.
report_archive_justification: The report history is publicly archived and searchable in GitHub Issues. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian/issues
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents the vulnerability reporting process, including an explicit scope and threat model for a static-data project. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Vulnerabilities are reported privately through GitHub private security advisories or by email to schuuby@proton.me, not via public issues. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to an initial response within a few days.
build_justification: The tooling builds from source with common FLOSS tools: `npm ci` then `npm run build` (tsc), and the dataset is regenerated with the documented `npm run` pipeline (reextract-binaries, backfill-binary, fetch-docs, scrape).
build_common_tools_justification: It is built with common, widely available FLOSS tools (Node.js, npm, TypeScript, tsx, vitest).
build_floss_tools_justification: All build and pipeline tooling (Node.js, npm, TypeScript, tsx, vitest) is FLOSS.
test_justification: An automated test suite runs with `npm test` (vitest), offline.
test_invocation_justification: Tests run with the standard `npm test`, documented in CONTRIBUTING.md. https://github.com/schubydoo/claustodian/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_most_justification: The suite covers most of the code, enforced by a CI-blocking vitest coverage floor of 95% statements, 95% lines, 95% functions, and 90% branches.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs the full suite, plus schema validation, on every pull request and on pushes to main.
test_policy_justification: Adding tests for new functionality is expected, backed by the merge-blocking coverage floor.
tests_are_added_justification: New functionality is added with tests; the coverage floor blocks merges that would drop coverage below the threshold.
tests_documented_added_justification: The test-and-validation policy is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md.
warnings_justification: TypeScript strict type-checking (`tsc --noEmit`), ESLint, and a prettier --check formatting gate run in CI.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any type error, lint error, or formatting difference, so warnings cannot merge to main.
warnings_strict_justification: Type, lint, and format checks are treated as errors (CI-blocking); the build is rejected on any finding.
know_secure_design_justification: The design is secure by construction: the deliverable is static data with no server, database, authentication, or runtime user input. The threat model in SECURITY.md focuses on what is actually in scope - dataset integrity, provenance, supply chain, and XSS in the rendered site - and the pipeline applies least privilege (GitHub Actions use SHA-pinned actions and OIDC rather than stored credentials) and verifies downloaded binaries by checksum.
know_common_errors_justification: The tooling is written in TypeScript (memory-safe). The one plausible runtime vulnerability class - XSS in site/index.html via upstream-derived descriptions - is called out in SECURITY.md, and CodeQL, gitleaks, zizmor, OSV-Scanner, and dependency review enforce common-error checks in CI.
crypto_published_justification: The project implements no cryptography of its own. Transport security is provided by GitHub and Cloudflare (HTTPS), and integrity of downloaded release binaries is verified with SHA-256 checksums via standard tooling.
crypto_call_justification: No cryptographic functionality is implemented in project code; checksum verification and transport security are delegated to standard tools and the hosting platforms.
crypto_floss_justification: The project uses no bespoke cryptographic software; any cryptography involved is provided by FLOSS platform tooling (Node.js/OpenSSL, standard checksum utilities).
crypto_keylength_justification: The project generates no keys and configures no cryptographic key lengths.
crypto_working_justification: The project uses no cryptographic algorithm for security purposes in its own code; SHA-256 is used only for download-integrity verification via standard tooling.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No cryptographic algorithm with known serious weaknesses is used for security purposes.
crypto_pfs_justification: The project terminates no TLS of its own; transport security for the published site is handled by GitHub Pages and Cloudflare.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The project stores no passwords and has no user accounts or authentication.
crypto_random_justification: The project's own code generates no security-sensitive random values.
delivery_mitm_justification: The dataset is delivered to consumers over HTTPS (claustodian.dev via GitHub Pages/Cloudflare), and the pipeline downloads official Claude Code release binaries over HTTPS and verifies them by checksum, countering MITM during retrieval.
delivery_unsigned_justification: The documented way to consume the data is fetching over HTTPS from claustodian.dev; users are never directed to fetch data or code over HTTP.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no known unpatched vulnerabilities; dependencies are monitored with OSV-Scanner, GitHub dependency review, and GitHub security alerts, and updated promptly (well within 60 days).
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No unpatched critical vulnerabilities exist; the OpenSSF Scorecard Vulnerabilities check and code/dependency scanning run on pushes to main and on a schedule.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are committed; gitleaks and GitHub secret scanning run in CI, and the GitHub Actions workflows authenticate with OIDC and short-lived GitHub App tokens rather than stored secrets.
static_analysis_justification: Static analysis runs in CI: CodeQL (JavaScript/TypeScript), gitleaks, zizmor (GitHub Actions auditing), dependency review, OSV-Scanner, and OpenSSF Scorecard.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL targets common vulnerability classes for JavaScript/TypeScript.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Static-analysis findings are triaged and addressed; Scorecard findings are reviewed and either fixed or dismissed with a documented rationale.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every pull request and push, with CodeQL and Scorecard also on a scheduled basis.
dynamic_analysis_justification: The vitest suite exercises the real extractors against real Claude Code release bundles with assertions enabled on every CI run, catching extraction defects dynamically.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The tooling is written in TypeScript on Node.js, a memory-safe runtime; memory and behavior sanitizers for memory-unsafe languages do not apply.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The test suite exercises the code with assertions enabled throughout.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: There are no outstanding dynamic-analysis findings; the test suite passes on main.
